newsitem.title: TURKEY: BASKETBALL-EUROPE'S BEST GATHER TO PROMOTE CONTINENTAL GAME.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-EUROPE'S BEST GATHER TO PROMOTE CONTINENTAL GAME.

text.p: Top players gather in Istanbul later this month for a special East v West match aimed at boosting continental basketball and carving out a distinct image for the European game.
The inaugural "Eurostars" game, on December 30, will launch an annual celebration on the game on the continent, which has for so long been seen as the poor relation of the American NBA league.

"Of the 10 best European players, at least eight are playing in the United States -- we want our children to have heroes over here. Heroes they can see, they can touch," FIBA spokesman Florian Wanninger said on Thursday.

The squads for the "Eurostars" game were chosen through a poll conducted by 10 basketball magazines. All play in European leagues, although three of them are American. A player is categorised as eastern or western according to his league and not his nationality.
Wanninger said the "Eurostars" games, which will be played in a different European country at the end of every year, were not part of a campaign simply to copy the glitzy NBA:
"That is actually what we want to avoid. We do not necessarily want the singing and the dancing and all that -- we want Europe to have a game in its own style," Wanninger said.

Umit Tarhan, of Turkey's Ulker Spor club, which is co-organising the event, said FIBA had chosen Turkey because it had the fastest developing game in Europe and a pool of 30 million young people as potential stars of the future.

WEST - Ronny Bayer (Belgium, Sunair-Oostende), Yann Bonato (France, Limoges), Richard Dacoury (France, Racing Paris), Henning Harnisch (Germany, Alba Berlin), Conrad McRae (U.S., Teamsystem Bologna), Carlton Myers (Italy, Teamsystem Bologna), Sasa Obradovic (Yugoslavia, Alba Berlin), Zeljko Rebraca (Yugoslavia, Benetton Treviso), Antoine Rigaudeau (France, Pau-Orthez), Delaney Rudd (U.S., Villeurbanne), Stefano Rusconi (Italy, Benetton Treviso), Zoran Savic (Yugoslavia, Virtus Bologna)

EAST - Serguei Bazarevich (Russia, CSKA-Moscow), Orhun Ene (Turkey, Ulker Spor), Panagiotis Fassoulas (Greece, Olympiakos), Evgueny Kissurine (Russia, Cibona Zagreb), Ibrahim Kutluay (Turkey, Fenerbahce), Petar Naumoski (Turkey, Efes Pilsen), David Rivers (U.S., Olympiakos), George Sigalas (Greece, Olympiakos), Dragan Tarlach (Greece, Olympiakos), Randy White (U.S., Maccabi-Tel Aviv), Jurij Zdovc (Slovenia, Iraklis-Thessalonika)
